title: three.ws MCP trust policy
description: The JSON document served by GET https://three.ws/api/mcp-policy (format=json). It sorts every tool in the three.ws MCP catalog into allow / confirm / deny buckets for the requested trust profile, so an MCP client can automate exactly the tools whose readOnlyHint has been verified against the handler that implements it. Docs: https://three.ws/docs/mcp-safety

profile.description: Which trust ladder rung this policy was generated for. balanced is the default.

summary.description: One-paragraph statement of what this profile automates and what it gates.

issuer.description: Origin that generated and signed off on the policy.

source.description: The tool catalog this policy was derived from (https://three.ws/mcp-catalog.json). The policy is regenerated from it on every request, so it always reflects the deployed tools.

method.description: How the safety labels behind this policy were established.

check.description: The repo command that re-verifies every label.

claim.description: What the verification guarantees about the labels.

total.description: Total tools in the catalog; equals allow + confirm + deny.

allow.description: Tools the client may run without asking under this profile.

confirm.description: Tools the client must ask about before running.

deny.description: Tools the client must refuse to run under this profile.

name.description: The tool name as it appears in tools/list.

permission.description: Namespaced permission id (mcp__<server>__<tool>) as MCP clients write it in their permission lists. The server segment is the id three.ws publishes; a client that named the server differently in its own config must substitute its own name.

server.description: The three.ws-published server id the tool belongs to.

safety.description: Verified safety class of the tool handler: read never changes state, write changes state reversibly, irreversible cannot be undone (signs, sends, settles, or deletes).

priceUsd.description: Price per call in USD. 0 means free.
